exam.title: Red Hat Certified Developer in AI
exam.study_prerequisites: Red Hat recommends DO288 or comparable OpenShift application experience plus AI267 or comparable OpenShift AI experience. Practice one reproducible OpenShift AI 3.3 lifecycle on OpenShift 4.20 across projects, workbenches, connections, placement, KServe/OpenVINO/vLLM serving, registry, TrustyAI and hardware monitoring, pipelines, model selection/compression/LMEval, Git/model development, and bounded streaming, RAG, agentic and guardrailed applications.

review.notes: All 12 unweighted EX267 groups were reconciled with OpenShift AI 3.3 on OpenShift 4.20. The repeated deploy/store group is mapped as a model-serving refinement, not an invented weight. Three scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks cover the complete governed lifecycle, failure evidence, persistence and rollback. All ten URLs are cataloged: eight reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. Older and rolling material has a 3.3/4.20 gap checklist; no gated course labs or recalled exam tasks are used.

findings.title: Main page and version PDF task coverage differ
findings.evidence: Main page has 43 tasks including selectors/tolerations and specific-node placement; EX267V33K in the public PDF has 41 otherwise matching tasks.
findings.recommendation: Keep the support limitation visible pending authoritative evidence.

findings.title: Standard/Advanced exam terminology lacks a verified product mapping
findings.evidence: Current 3.3 deployment book describes RawDeployment and Advanced settings; these words do not prove correspondence to older Standard/Advanced modes.
findings.recommendation: Keep the support limitation visible pending authoritative evidence.

findings.title: Hardware allocation needed version-specific explanation
findings.evidence: Hardware Profiles supersede Accelerator Profiles/legacy sizes and configure workload resource/placement fields.
findings.recommendation: Explain profiles versus actual allocatable resources and add a scheduling diagnosis matrix.
findings.resolution: Explain profiles versus actual allocatable resources and add a scheduling diagnosis matrix.

findings.title: Exam-listed optimization feature was not labeled with its support state
findings.evidence: 3.3 release notes list LLM Compressor integration as Developer Preview and distinguish current APIs/annotations from deprecated forms.
findings.recommendation: Retain optimization scope but explicitly label the preview and update connection/registry/profile guidance.
findings.resolution: Retain optimization scope but explicitly label the preview and update connection/registry/profile guidance.

findings.title: Registry metadata does not imply artifact storage or arbitrary URI deployment
findings.evidence: Model registry records metadata; the documented URI-registered deployment path supports public OCI repositories only.
findings.recommendation: Separate metadata access, artifact access and direct-serving workflows; bind accepted versions to immutable payloads.
findings.resolution: Separate metadata access, artifact access and direct-serving workflows; bind accepted versions to immutable payloads.

findings.title: Pipeline compilation and cache behavior needed executable evidence
findings.evidence: 3.3 docs support plain IR and Kubernetes-native output; hidden mutable input can invalidate the meaning of a reused result.
findings.recommendation: Compile an original typed-artifact graph in both formats with pinned SDK, explicit cache choices and resources; test input/digest/cohort failure cases locally.
findings.resolution: Compile an original typed-artifact graph in both formats with pinned SDK, explicit cache choices and resources; test input/digest/cohort failure cases locally.

findings.title: Evaluation access controls and dataset completeness were too abstract
findings.evidence: Platform permit settings and per-job allow settings independently control online resources and code execution; missing/undersized cohorts can undermine aggregate quality evidence.
findings.recommendation: Explain the two-level access boundary and include explicit expected-cohort/size criteria in the original synthetic exercise.
findings.resolution: Explain the two-level access boundary and include explicit expected-cohort/size criteria in the original synthetic exercise.

findings.title: Guardrail endpoint availability is not proof the guarded path ran
findings.evidence: Detectors, Orchestrator and gateway presets have separate configuration and observation boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Require intended-path, safe-label/threshold, dependency-failure and streaming tests with destination-scoped credential handling.
findings.resolution: Require intended-path, safe-label/threshold, dependency-failure and streaming tests with destination-scoped credential handling.
